method: Composite of fundamentals (25%), valuation (20%), technicals (20%), catalyst (20%) and smart money (15%). Technicals and, where a reverse-DCF applies, valuation are computed from the Fri 2026-10-02 close; the rest are analyst judgement.

names.note: Made a new all-time high on Friday and is only 1.7% below it at the close. The soft jobs data took Fed-hike odds from ~64% to ~16-23%, which helps the highest-quality AI name most, and it still trades on a modest forward multiple versus its growth.

The best catalyst in the book this week: a $1.2bn AI-rack order plus a better networking outlook, an upgrade and a target raise on the same day. It closed at 69.33, just 1.4% under its 70.29 high, still on a value multiple.

The foundry for every leading AI chip is pressing its 52-week high (479) while the broader market slipped. Micron's plan to raise fiscal 2027 capex and AMD's new Helios order both mean more leading-edge wafers.

Still the volume leader in AI servers with a $95bn backlog, and Friday's +3.84% shows buyers defend it on dips. The stock went nowhere on the week while HPE took the headlines — that is digestion, not damage, at 5.5% under the high.

The highest-quality franchise in the book (Azure +43%, 30m Copilot seats) held flat in a down week for the S&P — defensive strength inside tech. Nothing new to chase, which is exactly why it can be built slowly.

The Muse agent story is intact and analysts keep raising targets, yet the stock fell -3.1% this week with communication services. That is the digestion we flagged last week — it now sits 6.6% under its 779.819 high with sentiment cooler.
A sharp reversal: last week Bernstein cut it, this week it rallied +7.6% to near its high as security spending is treated as AI-proof. The chart now leads the fundamentals.
The EUV monopoly is finally moving with the AI trade: +7.1% this week as memory makers raise capex. Still 6.6% below its 1999.96 high, so there is room before the old peak.

AMD's Helios rack just landed a $1.2bn customer order through HPE — proof the MI-series is a real second source, not a slide. The stock is within 1.8% of its 645.46 high after crossing $1T last month.

The numbers were huge — $54bn of quarterly revenue and an 87% margin — and the guide was bigger again, yet the stock fell because the margin guide was 'only' 86.3%. Management calls FQ1 the margin floor for fiscal 2027 and is raising capex, which says demand runs into 2027-28.

Best-in-class AI Ethernet with net cash, sitting 3.5% below its high. HPE/Juniper's upgraded networking outlook this week is a competitive read-across, but it also confirms that AI networking budgets are growing.
Category leader at a fresh record: +7.1% this week as investors pay up for AI-era security. The flag is the President's $64m sale into the high — the business is strong, the entry is not.

Healthcare was the worst sector this week (about -2.7%), yet AbbVie barely moved and sits 2.4% from its high. Skyrizi/Rinvoq have replaced Humira and the cash flow funds a growing dividend — the defensive anchor of the healthcare group.
The largest US grid contractor with record backlog, up +4.2% this week and still 14.2% below its high. Power-grid spend is non-discretionary for the AI build-out.

worst.note: Custom AI silicon plus a VMware software annuity, but the stock keeps lagging the group — 28.3% below its high while TSM and NVDA press records.

New to the book as a value idea: Deutsche Bank upgraded it to Buy at ~18x its 2027 earnings, and the reverse-DCF needs only ~10% a year of FCF growth. The catch is the chart — it is sitting near its 52-week low.
Great business, broken chart: 35.1% below its high with healthcare money leaving. It stays in the book as a value-quality name, not a momentum one.
Premier franchise, wrong tape: financials are ~6% below their 50-day average and Q3 trading comparisons are hard. Kept as the second financial, not a buy candidate this week.
Best nuclear assets in the US, but the sector is being de-rated by 5%+ yields. Kept for the watch, not for buying.
Merchant power with more leverage than CEG, sitting near its low. A rate-relief rally candidate if long yields finally fall — not before.
